citations.title: Employee Qualifications and Training
citations.requirement: (a) The facility designates a manager in writing. The manager must be on duty 40 hrs/week and may manage only one facility, except a small Type A manager may oversee up to 4 facilities with no more than 16 residents in total. A backup is named in writing. Large-facility managers need an associate's degree, a bachelor's degree, or a high school credential plus 1 year of management experience. The manager completes a 24-hr ALF management course by the first anniversary, including 8 hrs on the standards within 3 months, plus 12 hrs of CE a year. (b) An attendant is in the facility whenever residents are present. (c) Staffing policies set ratios from residents' service plans. The normal 24-hr staffing pattern is disclosed before admission and posted monthly. Night staff: small Type A immediately available; large Type A and all Type B immediately available and awake. (d) 4-hr orientation for all staff. 16 hrs of attendant on-the-job training in the first 16 hrs after orientation. 6 hrs/yr of direct-care education, including 1 hr fall prevention and 1 hr behavior management. Annual geriatric in-service for nurses, CNAs and medication aides.

citations.title: Training Requirements for Staff Providing Personal Care Services to a Resident With Alzheimer's Disease or a Related Disorder in a Facility that is Not an Alzheimer's Certified Facility
citations.requirement: Manager: 4 hrs of training plus a competency evaluation, then 2 hrs of annual CE. Personal care staff: 4 hrs plus a competency evaluation before performing personal care, then 2 hrs of CE. Non-direct staff with recurring contact (housekeeping, front desk, maintenance) complete training and a competency evaluation on Alzheimer's disease, person-centered care and behaviors. Certificates are issued to staff and kept per records retention policy. Training carries over if the employment gap is under 2 years.

citations.title: All Staff Policy for Residents with Alzheimer's Disease or a Related Disorder
citations.requirement: Requires a facility policy on all staff and residents with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders. Section number and title verified from the Subchapter E table of contents, and §553.254(a)(2) confirms the §553.254 training may satisfy it. The full text was not retrieved, so confirm the policy's required content against the rule before finalizing.

citations.title: Human Resources
citations.requirement: Personnel files hold: criminal history check documentation; annual Employee Misconduct Registry (EMR) and Nurse Aide Registry (NAR) checks; TB screening; vaccine-policy compliance or exemption; the signed statement on criminal liability for failure to report; and a signed disclosure statement on §250.006 convictions and residence in another state in the past 5 years. Before hire, search the EMR and NAR. Do not hire or keep anyone listed as unemployable or convicted of a barring offense. Repeat searches at least every 12 months. A name-based criminal check is required in each prior state of residence in the past 5 years; the person may be hired pending results but not in a direct-contact position. Suspend, and do not reinstate, an employee HHSC finds engaged in reportable conduct until appeals are exhausted. Reportable conduct includes abuse or neglect causing harm, sexual abuse, financial exploitation of $25 or more, and emotional or verbal abuse causing harm.

citations.title: Admission Policies and Procedures
citations.requirement: (a) Do not admit or retain a resident whose needs cannot be met. Use a written admission agreement. Give the disclosure statement and rate schedule. Provide the Memory Care Disclosure Statement if memory care is marketed (plus HHSC Form 3641 if Alzheimer's certified). Physician exam within 30 days before or 14 days after admission. Collect the listed identifying information. (b) Comprehensive assessment and service plan within 14 days of admission. Update the plan annually and on significant change. (c) Give the disclosure statement before admission and the Resident's Bill of Rights. Give and document family receipt of the HHSC abuse hotline number. Keep written resident policies and give notice of changes before they take effect. Give the restraint/seclusion notice and the emergency plan or evacuation summary. (d) Advance directive policy and notice. $500 penalty for failure to inform. (e) Inappropriate placement: Forms 1124, 1125, 1126 within 10 working days; evacuation waiver; discharge within 30 days if the facility will not retain.

citations.title: Coordination of Care
citations.requirement: (a) Medication administration, supervision, self-administration, storage and disposal. (b) Accident, injury and acute illness response and documentation; first aid supplies. (c) Health care professionals and outside HCSSA services; no ongoing nursing-facility-level services. (d) Activity program at least weekly. (e) Dietary services. (f) Infection prevention and control, TB screening and the vaccine policy. (g) Restraints and seclusion (the heading was verified, but the subsection text was cut off in the retrieved copy; review it before finalizing).

citations.title: Health maintenance activities
citations.requirement: Personal care staff may perform a health maintenance activity (HMA) without delegation only when an RN has assessed and documented that it qualifies. The resident or representative must direct the task and agree in writing, and the condition must be stable and predictable. The RN reassesses on any change of condition, at least annually, and at least every 6 months for residents with Alzheimer's or in a certified facility or unit. Activities that are not HMAs require RN delegation under 22 TAC Chapter 225 and §553.261(a)(1)(A)(iii).

citations.title: Resident Records and Retention
citations.requirement: Records are confidential and safeguarded. A record contains the admission form, assessments, service plan, physician orders, advance directives, the physician exam, professional service documentation, and guardianship papers. Records are available to residents, legal representatives and HHSC. Keep a simple financial record of charges and of any personal funds handled. Issue receipts on request. Request the guardianship court order and letters at admission and at each annual assessment, make a follow-up request within 30 days, and keep the results.

citations.title: Rights
citations.requirement: (a) Give each resident the Residents' Bill of Rights and post it in each resident's primary language. The rights include freedom from abuse and from restraint used for discipline or convenience, restraint only on written physician authorization or in an emergency, and complaint without reprisal. They also include unopened mail, visitors at any reasonable hour, managing one's own finances with at least quarterly accounting, record access, choice of physician, participation in the service plan, refusal of treatment, a locked personal area, notice by day 30 of Medicare/Medicaid entitlement, discharge only on listed grounds with 30 days' written notice, and ombudsman access. (b) Post the Providers' Bill of Rights. A provider may terminate for just cause on 30 days' written notice, or immediately for a serious threat after notice to HHSC at 1-800-458-9858. (c) Allow HHSC access. (d) Authorized electronic monitoring (AEM).

citations.title: Access to Residents and Records by the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
citations.requirement: The State Ombudsman, certified ombudsmen and interns get immediate, private, unimpeded access to the facility and to residents during business or visiting hours. The State Ombudsman and certified ombudsmen also get access at other times if circumstances require. They get access to resident records with consent or as the rule otherwise allows. HIPAA does not bar release to the ombudsman, who is a health oversight agency.

citations.title: Postings
citations.requirement: Post in a public area: the license; the HHSC complaint-procedure sign; the notice that inspection reports are available and the HHSC toll-free number; the most recent inspection report; the Residents' Bill of Rights; the Providers' Bill of Rights; the local ombudsman number and the 1-800-252-2412 toll-free number; the normal 24-hr staffing pattern; and the sign 'Cases of Suspected Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation must be reported to HHSC by calling 1-800-458-9858.'

citations.title: Advertisements, Solicitations, and Promotional Material
citations.requirement: Rules on advertising and promotional material. Section number and title verified from the Subchapter E table of contents. The text was not retrieved, so draft the policy after reading the rule. Note §553.259(a)(4) on memory care marketing.

citations.title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation Reportable to HHSC by Facilities
citations.requirement: Staff with cause to believe a resident has been or may be harmed by abuse, neglect or exploitation, or died from abuse or neglect, report to HHSC at 1-800-458-9858 (or the HHSC website) and to municipal police or the county sheriff. The report includes the resident's name, age and address, the responsible person, the nature of the condition, the basis of knowledge, and other relevant information. The facility makes an immediate oral report, investigates, and sends a written investigation report to the HHSC state office no later than the 5th calendar day after the oral report. No retaliation. Staff sign a statement, as a condition of employment, that they may be criminally liable for failure to report. The facility follows its internal prevention, detection and reporting policies.

citations.title: Emergency Preparedness and Response
citations.requirement: Document a risk assessment (fire, outage, flood, hurricane or severe weather, epidemic, cyber attack, etc.). Keep a written plan covering the 8 core functions: direction and control, warning, communication, sheltering, evacuation, transportation, health and medical needs, and resource management. Coordinate with the local Emergency Management Coordinator. Designate an Emergency Preparedness Coordinator and an alternate. Review and update the plan annually and within 30 days after an event, drill shortcoming or rule change. Give residents and representatives the plan or an evacuation summary at admission. Register with 2-1-1 Texas and tell residents how to register for evacuation assistance. Shelter-in-place temperatures must be 68–82°F. Notify the HHSC regional office and the EMC on a decision to shelter or evacuate. Keep written acknowledgments with a receiving facility and an alternate. Plan for pets and service animals. Only subsections (a)–(i)(2)(D)(i) were retrieved; review the remaining subsections (staff accompaniment, training, drills, return) before finalizing.

citations.title: Types of Assisted Living Facilities
citations.requirement: Type A: residents can evacuate without staff help, with no routine night attendance. Type B: residents may need evacuation help and night attendance but may not be permanently bedfast.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Small facility: licensed for 16 or fewer residents. Large facility: 17 or more. Defines terms used in the staffing, HMA, infection control and AEM rules.

citations.title: Licensing criteria, general application requirements, time periods, initial license procedures
citations.requirement: Initial application through the HHSC portal (TULIP) with the local fire authority documentation and the pre-licensure training certificate. A Life Safety Code inspection and a health inspection are required. After the LSC inspection, 1–3 residents may be admitted. HHSC must deny an applicant whose health care or long-term care license was revoked within the last 5 years or who is excluded from Medicare/Medicaid (§553.17). Applications still incomplete 120 days after receipt are denied (§553.21).

citations.title: License Fees
citations.requirement: 3-year license fee of $300 + $15 per bed, capped at $2,250. Alzheimer's certification +$300. $15 per bed for a capacity increase. Late-renewal fee of half the basic fee if filed later than 45 days before expiration. Possible trust fund assessment (§553.47(d)). Expedited LSC inspection fee (§553.47(g)).

citations.title: Facility Construction; Fire Protection Systems for New Small Type A / Type B Facilities
citations.requirement: Construction and life safety standards in separate divisions for existing and new facilities, small and large, Type A and Type B. New small Type A and Type B facilities need an NFPA 13, 13R or 13D sprinkler system with electrical supervision, and a manual fire alarm with smoke detection (§§553.215, 553.225). Residents' evacuation capability must match the NFPA 101 and Subchapter D requirements (§553.259(a)(1)).

citations.title: Additional Licensing Standards for Certified Alzheimer's Assisted Living Facilities
citations.requirement: Added staffing, training, admission, disclosure (Form 3641) and physical plant standards (§553.311) for an Alzheimer's certified facility or unit. Certification applies to Type B only (§553.27).

citations.title: Inspections, Investigations, and Informal Dispute Resolution
citations.requirement: HHSC inspections and complaint investigations, and the informal dispute resolution process. Section range verified from the Chapter 553 table of contents; text not retrieved.

citations.title: Enforcement
citations.requirement: Enforcement remedies, including administrative penalties, license actions and plans of correction. Subchapter verified from the Chapter 553 table of contents; text not retrieved.

citations.title: Nurse Aide Registry and Criminal History Checks for Facility Employees
citations.requirement: Verify employability through criminal history and registry checks, with an annual registry search. §250.006 lists the convictions that bar employment (referenced in §553.257).

citations.title: Assisted Living Facility Licensing Act
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for ALF licensure by HHSC, including plan review (§247.0261, per HHSC guidance).

citations.title: STAR+PLUS Home and Community Based Services (HCBS) Program
citations.requirement: STAR+PLUS HCBS eligibility and interest-list rules for members who may receive assisted living services.

citations.title: STAR+PLUS Handbook – Assisted Living Services
citations.requirement: Housing options (apartment vs non-apartment) are stated in the MCO contract. Members live in an ALF contracted with their MCO. Health assessment and emergency training within 3 days of admission. At least 4 social activities a week. Next-business-day reporting of changes to the MCO. Member trust fund records. Room and board cannot be waived (a lower amount may be accepted), is prorated in the first month, and is due on a written date.

citations.title: Medication services in assisted living facilities
citations.requirement: HHSC guidance on medication administration, supervision and self-administration. Only a licensed nurse, a permitted medication aide under a nurse on duty or on call, or an RN-delegated employee may administer medications. A medication aide permit takes 100 classroom + 20 lab + 10 clinical hours and an exam, with annual renewal.

citations.title: State responsibilities – screening and enrollment of managed care network providers
citations.requirement: Managed care network providers, including STAR+PLUS ALFs, must be screened and enrolled with the State.

citations.title: Alzheimer's certification of a Type B facility or unit; license renewal; capacity change
citations.requirement: Only a Type B facility or unit may be Alzheimer's certified (§553.27). Renew the license on time (§553.33). Get HHSC approval before adding beds (§553.39). Sections are present in the research section list; text not re-fetched.

citations.title: Community Homes for Disabled Persons Location Act
citations.requirement: An ALF licensed under HSC Ch. 247 can qualify as a community home. Up to 6 persons with disabilities + 2 supervisors. No community home within one-half mile of another.

citations.title: Ombudsman access to facilities, residents and records
citations.requirement: Federal basis for the ombudsman's access rights, as incorporated in 26 TAC §553.269(b)–(c).

policies.title: Organization, Licensee and Manager Responsibilities
state_specifics: The facility designates a manager in writing with authority over operations (§553.253(a)).

Manager must be on duty 40 hrs/week and may manage only one facility. Exception: a small Type A manager may have up to 4 facilities with no more than 16 residents in total and must be reachable by phone or pager off-site.
Name in writing an employee competent and authorized to act in the manager's absence.

Manager qualifications: small facility, high school diploma or equivalent; large facility (17+), associate's degree (nursing, health care management or related), bachelor's degree, or high school credential plus 1 year of management experience.

Manager training: 24-hr ALF management course, with 8 hrs on the standards within 3 months of hire, completed by the first anniversary. Facility in-services do not count. Keep evidence of content, hours, dates and provider. An exemption applies for a comparable prior course, or for a manager moving between licensed ALFs with a break of 30 days or less.
Manager CE: 12 hrs per year covering at least two of the listed areas. Also 4 hrs of Alzheimer's/dementia training with a competency test, then 2 hrs per year (§553.254(b)).
Document the license category (Type A or B; small ≤16 or large 17+) and the evacuation capability of every resident against it.

policies.title: Licensure, Renewal and Regulatory Compliance
state_specifics: The license is HHSC LTCR Type A or Type B, issued for 3 years. Fee is $300 + $15 per bed, capped at $2,250. Alzheimer's certification adds $300.
File renewal at least 45 days before expiration. A later filing adds a late fee of half the basic fee (§553.47(b)).
Get HHSC approval before adding beds ($15 per added bed, and the building must meet construction rules) (§§553.39, 553.47(a)(2)).
Applications and changes are filed through TULIP on HHSC Form 3720 (3721 adds Alzheimer's certification).
HHSC may assess an annual trust fund fee, payable within 90 days of notice (§553.47(d)).
HHSC contacts: Licensing 512-438-2630, LTC_ALF_ICF_Licensing@hhs.texas.gov; LTCR Policy 512-438-3161, LTCRPolicy@hhs.texas.gov; complaint and incident intake 800-458-9858.
Facilities of 6 or fewer residents that rely on community-home status (HRC Ch. 123) keep zoning and half-mile spacing documentation on file.
Surveys cover the Life Safety Code and health inspections. Subchapter G covers investigations and informal dispute resolution. Subchapter H covers enforcement.

policies.title: Policy Review, Document Control and Rule Change Tracking
state_specifics: Written resident policies must be available to staff and to residents or responsible parties at admission. Notify residents of any policy change in writing before its effective date (§553.259(c)(4)–(5)).

The emergency plan, evacuation summary and contact lists are reviewed at least annually. Update them within 30 days after a disaster shortcoming, a drill shortcoming, or a change in facility policy or HHSC rule, and document the review date and changes (§553.275(d)).

Track HHSC rule changes. A proposed Chapter 553 revision (Proposed Rule 25R031, Texas Register, Sept. 4, 2026) would change on-duty staffing, add food handler and infection-control training, and renumber sections. It is proposed, not adopted; update citations when it is adopted.

policies.title: Quality Assurance, Plans of Correction and Survey Response
state_specifics: Chapter 553 as retrieved does not prescribe a QAPI program for ALFs. This is a facility-adopted policy built on the rule-driven review points.

Survey response uses HHSC Form 3724 (Statement of Licensing Violations and Plan of Correction) and Form 3614-A (Report of Contact). Placement-related submissions are due within 10 working days of receiving them (§553.259(e)).

Review points: drill shortcomings corrected within 30 days (§553.275(d)(2)(C)); annual resident assessment and service plan review; incident and abuse report trends; infection data; resident grievances.
Informal dispute resolution is available under Subchapter G.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: HHSC must deny a license to an applicant or controlling person excluded from Medicare/Medicaid or with a license revoked in the past 5 years (§553.17). Screen owners and staff against exclusion lists.
STAR+PLUS ALFs are screened and enrolled and contract with MCOs. Bill the correct HCPCS T2031 level code and verify each MCO's billing guide.
Keep the simple financial record of charges billed to each resident, available to HHSC (§553.265(b)). Issue receipts on request.
STAR+PLUS room and board can be reduced but not waived (Handbook §§7240–7241.1).

policies.title: Required Postings and Providers' Bill of Rights
state_specifics: Post in a public area readily available to residents, employees and visitors: license; HHSC complaint sign; inspection-report availability notice with the HHSC toll-free number; latest inspection report; Residents' Bill of Rights (in each resident's primary language); Providers' Bill of Rights; local ombudsman number and 1-800-252-2412; 24-hr staffing pattern (updated monthly); abuse sign with 1-800-458-9858.
Post the 8½ x 11 'Electronic Monitoring' notice at the main entrance (§553.267(d)(7)).
Advertising and promotional material must comply with §553.272. If memory care is marketed, give the Memory Care Disclosure Statement.

policies.title: Resident Rights and Responsibilities (Residents' Bill of Rights)
state_specifics: Give every resident a copy of the Residents' Bill of Rights at admission and post it (§§553.259(c)(2), 553.267(a)(1)).

Rights cover mail, visits at any reasonable hour, a telephone, privacy, choice of physician, refusal of treatment, a locked personal area, finances, access to records, and temporary or permanent departure.
Residents are told by the 30th day after admission whether they are entitled to Medicare or Medicaid benefits and which items and services are covered (§553.267(a)(3)(W)).
A married couple receiving similar services may share a room.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: A resident may complain about care or treatment anonymously or through a designee. The provider must respond promptly and may not discriminate or retaliate (§553.267(a)(3)(H), §553.273(e)).
Post the HHSC complaint sign and the toll-free number. HHSC complaints and incident intake: 800-458-9858.
Complaints about abuse, neglect or exploitation follow the SAF-01 policy, not an internal grievance track.

policies.title: Ombudsman Access
state_specifics: The State Ombudsman, certified ombudsmen and interns have immediate, private, unimpeded access to the facility and residents at regular business or visiting hours. The State Ombudsman and certified ombudsmen may also enter at other times if circumstances require.
Release records to the ombudsman per §553.269(c). The ombudsman is a health oversight agency, so HIPAA does not bar release.
Post the local ombudsman number and 1-800-252-2412.

policies.title: Admission Agreement, Fees, Deposits and Refunds
state_specifics: A written admission agreement states the services and charges. If any service or supply could be a Medicare benefit, give the resident a statement saying so (§553.259(a)(2)).

Written policies must cover residents accepted, services, charges, refunds, responsibilities, privileges and rules (§553.259(c)(4)). Give the facility disclosure statement and rate schedule before admission and document receipt (§553.259(c)(1)).

Provider termination for just cause needs 30 days' written notice. Immediate termination for a serious or immediate threat needs notice to HHSC (1-800-458-9858 on evenings, weekends and holidays) (§553.267(b)(2)).
STAR+PLUS room and board is capped by the SSI rate minus the $85 personal needs allowance (2026: $909/month). It is prorated in the first month and due on a written date (Handbook §§7240–7241.1).

policies.title: Resident Funds and Personal Property
state_specifics: The resident may manage their own money or authorize another person in writing. The resident chooses the manner (money management program, representative payee, financial POA, trust, or similar) and may choose the least restrictive.
If the facility accepts written delegation to handle funds, give the resident an accounting at least quarterly and on request.
Keep a simple financial record of receipts and expenditures, available to HHSC. Issue receipts for payments on request (§553.265(b)).
Residents keep and use personal property and have a locked area in their living quarters (§553.267(a)(3)(S),(U)).
STAR+PLUS member trust fund records are kept per Handbook §§7250–7252.

policies.title: Advance Directives
federal: 42 CFR 489.102 (not applicable to ALFs; state rule governs)
state_specifics: Maintain written policies on implementing advance directives, including a clear statement of any procedure the facility is unwilling or unable to provide or withhold (§553.259(d)(1)).

Give written notice at admission. If the resident is incapacitated, give notice in order of preference: guardian, person responsible for health care decisions, spouse, adult child, parent, person admitting the resident. Give notice again when the resident becomes able to receive it.
HHSC imposes a $500 administrative penalty for failure to inform residents. The facility has 20 days to consent or request a hearing.
Keep any advance directive in the resident record (§553.265(a)(2)(E)). Residents may execute one under HSC Chapter 166.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Resident records are confidential and safeguarded from unauthorized use, loss or destruction. Release only with consent, to another provider on transfer, or when another law requires it (§§553.265(a)(1), 553.267(a)(3)(M)).
Records are available to residents, legal representatives and HHSC.
Confidentiality is a required orientation topic for all staff (§553.253(d)(1)(B)).
Ombudsman and HHSC access are permitted disclosures.
Apply HIPAA to the extent the facility is a covered entity (for example, if it bills Medicaid electronically).

policies.title: Nondiscrimination, Language Access and Accessibility
federal: Fair Housing Act, 42 USC 3601 et seq.
state_specifics: Residents are treated with dignity regardless of race, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status or source of payment (§553.267(a)(3)(E)).
Residents may not be prohibited from speaking their native language with other residents or staff for treatment, care or services (§553.267(a)(3)(G)).
The Residents' Bill of Rights is posted in each resident's primary language (§553.267(a)(1)(B)). The comprehensive assessment records primary language (§553.259(b)(1)(B)).
Manager CE and the 24-hr course include ADA accessibility, the Fair Housing Act and other federal laws (§553.253(a)(2),(3)(H)).

policies.title: Authorized Electronic Monitoring (AEM)
state_specifics: The facility must permit electronic monitoring of a resident's room on request. It may not refuse admission or discharge a resident for requesting AEM (§553.267(d)(1)–(2)).
All new and current residents sign the HHSC 'Information Regarding Authorized Electronic Monitoring' form, kept in the active clinical record.

The request uses the HHSC Request for AEM form. The HHSC Consent to AEM form is also needed from every other resident in the room. Roommates may condition consent on pointing the camera away or limiting audio.
The resident or representative pays all costs. The facility must provide a secure mount and power access, and must obstruct the camera on request to protect dignity.
A notice at the room entrance is mandatory when AEM is in use. A facility-wide 'Electronic Monitoring' notice at the main entrance is mandatory regardless.
A physician determines capacity to request AEM, and the determination is documented. Surrogate priority order is in §553.267(d)(4)(C)(ii).
Abuse or neglect seen on a recording must be reported under §553.273. Covert monitoring is not a ground for discharge.

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening, Disclosure and Admission Criteria
state_specifics: Do not admit or retain a resident whose needs the facility cannot meet and who cannot secure services from an outside resource. Facility management decides, with the written concurrence of the resident, physician or legal representative (§553.259(a)(1)).
Type A: residents can evacuate without staff help. Type B: residents may need evacuation help but may not be permanently bedfast (§553.5).
Physician exam within 30 days before or 14 days after admission, unless a transferring hospital or facility has a physical exam in the record.

Collect at admission: full name, SSN, usual residence, sex, marital status, date and place of birth, usual occupation, emergency contacts and physician, pharmacy preference, Medicaid/Medicare number (§553.259(a)(6)).

Before admission: explain and give the disclosure statement; give the Residents' Bill of Rights; give and document the family's receipt of the HHSC abuse hotline number; give the restraint/seclusion notice; give the emergency plan or evacuation summary.
If memory care is promoted, give the Assisted Living Facility Memory Care Disclosure Statement, and HHSC Form 3641 if Alzheimer's certified.
Request guardianship order and letters at admission (§553.265(c)). Emergency admissions are assessed and given a service plan. Respite service plans may be kept for 6 months.

policies.title: Resident Assessment and Reassessment
state_specifics: A comprehensive assessment is completed within 14 days of admission, on a facility-developed form. If information cannot be obtained, document the attempts (§553.259(b)).

Required elements: admitting location, primary language, sleep, behaviors, psychosocial/depression screen, Alzheimer's history, ADL patterns, activity preferences, cognition, communication, physical function, continence, nutrition, oral/dental, diagnoses, medications (administered/supervised/self), health conditions and side effects, special treatments, hospital admissions in past 6 months, and preventive health needs.
Reassess annually and on significant change in condition.
The RN's HMA reassessment is at least annual, or every 6 months for residents with Alzheimer's/related disorders or in a certified facility (§553.263(b)(4)).
STAR+PLUS members also need a health assessment and emergency training within 3 days of admission (Handbook §§7250–7252).

policies.title: Individual Service Plan
state_specifics: The service plan is completed within 14 days of admission and based on the comprehensive assessment (§553.259(b)).
It is approved and signed by the resident or the person responsible for their health care decisions. The facility provides care according to the plan.
Update the plan annually and on significant change. The resident may participate in developing it (§553.267(a)(3)(O)).
Staffing ratios are based on needs identified in service plans (§553.253(c)(1)).

Share the disclosure statement, rate schedule and service plan with outside resources providing additional services. Outside resources provide their care plans and document services at the facility on the day provided (§553.259(a)(3)).
For STAR+PLUS members, coordinate with the MCO service plan (ISP) and its renewal cycle.

policies.title: Retention Limits and Conditions the Facility Cannot Serve
state_specifics: The facility may not provide ongoing services comparable to those of a licensed nursing facility (HSC Chapter 242) (§553.261(c)(1)).

'Aging in place' with outside services is allowed only with the written concurrence of the resident, physician or legal representative. The facility must still meet NFPA 101 and Subchapter D requirements for each resident's evacuation capability (§553.259(a)(1)).
A Type B facility may not retain a permanently bedfast resident (§553.5).
A provider may refuse a referral if inappropriate and may maintain a weapons- and drug-free environment (§553.267(b)(2)(H),(I)).
Before admission, determine whether the building and staffing can meet the resident's evacuation needs. Use ADM-05 if they cannot.

policies.title: Inappropriate Placement and Evacuation Waiver
state_specifics: Change of condition but still meeting evacuation criteria: to keep the resident, submit within 10 working days of HHSC's Form 3724 and Form 3614-A (or of the facility's own determination) the Physician's Assessment (Form 1126), the Resident's Request to Remain (Form 1125) and the Facility Request (Form 1124) (§553.259(e)(1)).

Facility does not meet the evacuation requirements for a designated resident: request an evacuation waiver from the HHSC regional office within 10 working days. If the facility is unwilling to retain the resident, discharge within 30 days after receiving Forms 3724 and 3614-A (§553.259(e)(2)).

Waiver packet: Forms 1126, 1125, 1124; detailed emergency plan (staff positions, night awake staff, evacuation training); floor plan; evacuation plan; 12 months of fire drill records; Fire Marshal Notification Form 1127; Fire Suppression Authority Notification Form 1129; assessment within 60 days; service plan; other residents' service plans if requested.

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Relocation Notice
state_specifics: Discharge or transfer is permitted only if: it is for the resident's welfare and needs cannot be met; the resident's health improved so services are no longer needed; the resident's health or safety, or another's, is endangered; the provider ceases operating or leaves the reimbursement program; or the resident fails to pay after reasonable notice (§553.267(a)(3)(X)).

Except in an emergency, give 30 days' written notice to the resident, legal representative or family member stating the intent, the reason, the effective date, the destination if any, and appeal rights (§553.267(a)(3)(Y)).
Provider-initiated immediate termination for a serious or immediate threat requires notice to HHSC (1-800-458-9858) (§553.267(b)(2)(C)).
Medications held in central storage are released to a discharged resident on a signed receipt (§553.261(a)(6)(C)).
Discharge cannot be based on a request for electronic monitoring (§553.267(d)(2)).

policies.title: STAR+PLUS HCBS Assisted Living Participation
state_specifics: Applies only if the facility contracts with STAR+PLUS MCOs. The MCO contract states which housing options are offered (apartment single or double, non-apartment). Non-apartment settings are freestanding buildings licensed for 16 or fewer beds.

Operational duties: health assessment and emergency training within 3 days of admission; at least 4 social activities a week; report changes to the MCO by the next business day; keep member trust fund records (Handbook §§7250–7252).
Room and board is SSI minus $85 ($909/month in 2026). It cannot be waived, only reduced, and is prorated in the first month. SSI recipients owe no copayment (§§7240–7241.1).
Bill HCPCS T2031 with the level modifier on the new ISP. Keep billing a member's current RUG-III code until the ISP renews (effective 9/1/2025 rate methodology).

policies.title: Medication Management, Storage and Disposal
state_specifics: Provide a locked area for all medications (central storage, medication cart, or resident room). Store each resident's medications separately (§553.261(a)(5)).
Refrigerated medications need a designated locked area unless the refrigerator is inside a locked medication room.
Store poisons and 'external use only' items separately within the locked medication area.
If controlled drugs are stored, policies must address prevention of diversion.

Discontinued, expired and deceased residents' medications are kept separate from current medications and disposed of by a Texas-licensed registered pharmacist (§553.261(a)(6)(A)). Needles and syringes follow 25 TAC §§1.131–1.137.
Prescriptions are dispensed by a pharmacy or the resident's treating physician or dentist. Physician samples need specific dosage instructions for the individual resident.

policies.title: Medication Administration and Staff Authorization
state_specifics: Medications are administered per physician orders. Residents who cannot or choose not to self-administer have medications given only by: (i) a currently licensed person authorized to administer, (ii) a medication aide with a current permit acting under a licensed nurse on duty or on call, or (iii) an employee delegated by an RN under 22 TAC Chapter 225 (§553.261(a)(1)(A)).
Medication aide permit: 100 classroom + 20 lab + 10 clinical hours and an exam. Renew yearly ($15). Seven hours of CE are required for renewals after the first.
Keep a medication profile record for each resident: name, strength, dosage, amount received, directions, route, prescription number, pharmacy, and date issued.
Report any unusual reaction to the physician and responsible party immediately.
Document every missed or refused dose: date, time, and medication name and strength (not required when the resident is away from the facility).
A nurse must be employed or on call (the model uses 4 hrs/week for a 6-bed home and 8 hrs/week for 16 beds, an operator estimate). Without one, admit only residents who self-administer.

policies.title: Medication Supervision and Resident Self-Administration
state_specifics: Supervision is limited to: reminders; opening containers and replacing lids; pouring the prescribed dose per the medication profile; returning medications to locked storage; obtaining medications from the pharmacy; and maintaining the medication profile record (§553.261(a)(2)).

Residents who keep medications locked in their room are counseled by staff at least monthly on whether they can still self-administer safely and keep medications secure. A written record is required (§553.261(a)(3)(A)).
A resident may access the central storage area to self-administer, with staff present the whole time (§553.261(a)(3)(B)).

policies.title: Nursing Services, RN Delegation and Health Maintenance Activities
state_specifics: Health care professionals may coordinate services within their scope of practice, but the facility must not provide ongoing nursing-facility-comparable services (§553.261(c)(1)).

Residents may contract with a home and community support services agency (Chapter 558 of this title) or an independent health professional (§553.261(c)(2)). Temporary illness or injury services may be delivered by qualified persons (§553.261(b)(3)).

HMA without delegation: only for a person with a functional disability. An RN must document an assessment, and the condition must be stable and predictable. The resident or representative must be able and willing to direct the task and agree in writing (§553.263).
If an activity is not an HMA, personal care staff may do it only through RN delegation under 22 TAC Chapter 225, and for medication under §553.261(a)(1)(A)(iii) (§553.263(d)).
RN reassessment: on any change of condition, at least annually, and at least every 6 months for residents with Alzheimer's/related disorder or in a certified facility or unit.

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: After an accident or injury needing emergency medical, dental or nursing care: arrange emergency care or transfer; immediately notify the physician and next of kin, responsible party or placing agency; document on a separate report with a statement of final disposition (§553.261(b)(1)).
Report unusual reactions to medications or treatments immediately to the physician and responsible party (§553.261(a)(4)(A)).
Update the service plan on significant change in condition (§553.259(b)(2)). Consider whether the resident is now inappropriately placed (ADM-05).
STAR+PLUS: report significant changes to the MCO by the next business day.
Stock first aid supplies for burns, cuts and poisoning in a single location (§553.261(b)(2)).

policies.title: Dementia and Memory Care
state_specifics: All facilities serving residents with Alzheimer's or related disorders must meet §553.254: personal care staff get 4 hrs of training and pass a competency evaluation before providing personal care, then 2 hrs of CE. Managers get 4 hrs plus 2 hrs/yr. Non-direct staff with recurring contact also complete training and an evaluation. Certificates are kept.
Keep the all-staff Alzheimer's policy required by §553.255 (confirm required content from the rule text).
If memory care is marketed, give the Memory Care Disclosure Statement. An Alzheimer's certified facility also gives HHSC Form 3641 (§553.259(a)(4)).
Certification is open only to Type B facilities or units (§553.27) and adds Subchapter F staffing, training and physical plant standards (§553.311). The fee is +$300 on Form 3721.
The RN HMA reassessment is every 6 months for these residents (§553.263(b)(4)(B)).
The emergency plan resident list must identify residents with Alzheimer's or related disorders (§553.275(c)(2)(C)).

policies.title: Falls Prevention
state_specifics: Direct care staff must complete 1 hr of competency-based fall prevention training each year as part of the 6 hrs of annual education (§553.253(d)(3)).
Attendants' 16-hr on-the-job training includes safety measures to prevent accidents and injuries, fall prevention, and emergency first aid for a resident who falls (§553.253(d)(2)).
Document each fall on a separate report with final disposition, and notify the physician and responsible party (§553.261(b)(1)).
Include fall risk in the comprehensive assessment and service plan (physical functioning and transfer status).

policies.title: Skin Integrity and Pressure Injury Prevention
state_specifics: Chapter 553 has no stand-alone skin integrity rule in the retrieved text. This policy implements the service plan, first aid and scope-of-care rules.
Assess nutrition, continence and physical functioning in the 14-day assessment (§553.259(b)(1)).

Wound or treatment care beyond personal care must be done by licensed or delegated persons: a licensed professional, an HCSSA or independent professional, or RN delegation or HMA assessment (§§553.261(c), 553.263).
Report sudden changes in condition to the physician and the responsible party (§553.261(a)(4), (b)).
Ongoing care comparable to a nursing facility is not permitted (§553.261(c)(1)).

policies.title: Hospice and Home Health Coordination
state_specifics: A resident may contract with a home and community support services agency licensed under Chapter 558 of the title, or an independent health professional, for services at the facility (§553.261(c)(2)).

Share the disclosure statement, rate schedule and service plan with outside resources. Outside providers must give the facility their care plans and document services at the facility on the day provided (§553.259(a)(3)).
Include HCSSAs and independent professionals in the emergency contact list and notification procedures (§553.275(g)(3)(C),(g)(5)(E)).
The facility remains responsible for all care provided at the facility (§553.259(a)(1)).

policies.title: Death of a Resident
state_specifics: On apparent death: arrange emergency care or transfer, immediately notify the physician and next of kin, responsible party or placing agency, and document on a report with final disposition (§553.261(b)(1)).
If the death is believed due to abuse or neglect, report to HHSC (1-800-458-9858) and law enforcement (§553.273(a)).
Medications remaining after a resident's death are separated and disposed of by a Texas-licensed pharmacist (§553.261(a)(6)(A)(ii)).
Resident funds and property are accounted for per the facility's financial record (§553.265(b)). Keep the record per REC-01.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Anyone with cause to believe a resident has been or may be harmed by abuse, neglect or exploitation, or died from abuse or neglect, reports to HHSC at 1-800-458-9858 and to municipal law enforcement or the county sheriff (§553.273(a)).
Oral report to HHSC is immediate. The facility investigates and sends a written report to the HHSC state office no later than the 5th calendar day after the oral report (§553.273(d)).
Report content: resident name, age and address; responsible person; nature and extent of the condition; basis of knowledge; other relevant information (§553.273(c)).
No retaliation against any person who files a complaint or provides information in good faith (§553.273(e)).
Every employee signs, as a condition of employment, a statement that they may be criminally liable for failure to report. Keep it in the personnel file (§553.273(f), §553.257(a)(6)).

Reportable-conduct suspension: when HHSC finds that an employee engaged in abuse, neglect, sexual abuse, financial exploitation of $25 or more, or harmful emotional abuse, suspend the employee and do not reinstate during appeals (§553.257(b)(8)–(9)).
Reporting abuse is a required orientation topic for all staff (§553.253(d)(1)(A)). Post the sign with 1-800-458-9858 (§553.271(9)).

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting
state_specifics: Document every accident, injury or acute illness on a separate report with a statement of final disposition, kept on file (§553.261(b)(1)(C)).
Notify the physician and next of kin, responsible party or placing agency immediately.
Reportable incidents are self-reported to HHSC through TULIP or Complaint and Incident Intake at 800-458-9858.
Report any resident with a reportable disease to the city, county or health unit authority immediately (§553.261(f)(3)).
Staff must be told which conditions to report to the manager (§553.253(d)(1)(D)).
Disasters and emergency decisions are reported under SAF-05.

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
state_specifics: Chapter 553 as retrieved has no stand-alone elopement rule. This policy implements the supervision and emergency requirements.
Staff must be sufficient to give each resident the supervision and care needed to meet basic needs. An attendant must be in the facility whenever residents are present (§553.253(b)(1),(c)(3)(E)).
Identify residents with Alzheimer's or related disorders and those needing special assistance on the emergency plan's resident list (§553.275(c)(2)(C)).
Certified Alzheimer's facilities follow Subchapter F physical plant and staffing standards (§553.311).

Document a missing-resident event on an incident report (§553.261(b)). If a resident is believed harmed by neglect, report under §553.273. Notify the resident's responsible party and physician immediately.

policies.title: Restraints and Restrictive Practices
state_specifics: Residents are free from physical and chemical restraints used for discipline or convenience (§553.267(a)(3)(A)).

Physical or chemical restraints may be used only with written physician authorization or in an emergency to protect the resident or others from injury. The authorization must specify the circumstances and duration. Except in an emergency, only qualified medical personnel may administer restraints.
For a resident with an intellectual disability and a court-appointed guardian, behavior modification involving restraints or adverse stimuli needs the guardian's informed consent (§553.267(a)(3)(D)).
Before or upon admission, notify the resident and representative of HHSC rules and facility policy on restraint and seclusion (§553.259(c)(6)).
Training: behavior management, de-escalation, practices to decrease restraint use, and alternatives to restraint (§553.253(d)(2)(F),(d)(3)).
§553.261(g) separately governs restraints and seclusion; read and incorporate its full text before finalizing.

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Disaster Plan
state_specifics: Document a risk assessment covering fire, outage, water contamination, wildfire, hazmat, active shooter or bomb threat, flood, hurricane or severe weather, epidemic or pandemic, cyber attack and loss of facility (§553.275(b)).
The written plan covers 8 core functions: direction and control, warning, communication, sheltering, evacuation, transportation, health and medical needs, and resource management (§553.275(c)).
Name an Emergency Preparedness Coordinator and an alternate. Document contact information for the local Emergency Management Coordinator and notify and coordinate with the EMC.

Keep a printed plan in a central location accessible to staff, residents and representatives. Give the plan or an evacuation summary at admission, on request and on significant change. Register the facility with 2-1-1 Texas and tell residents how to register for evacuation assistance.
Shelter in place: arrange safe power and temperatures of at least 68°F and no more than 82°F. Notify the HHSC regional office and EMC immediately after deciding to shelter or evacuate.
Evacuation: pre-arranged destination and a receiving facility with written acknowledgment, plus an alternate. Evacuate when the county judge or mayor orders it. Plan for pets and service animals.
Update the plan within 30 days after an event, drill or rule change. Only part of §553.275 was retrieved; check drill and training provisions in the full text.

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
state_specifics: New small Type A and Type B facilities must have an NFPA 13, 13R or 13D sprinkler system chosen per NFPA 101 Ch. 32, with electrical supervision (§§553.215(b), 553.225).

A manual fire alarm per NFPA 101 Ch. 9 with a whole-building evacuation alarm. Smoke detectors in bedrooms, corridors, living and dining rooms, offices, kitchens, laundries and common areas. Dedicated circuit with secondary power per NFPA 72.
Keep inspection and testing records for sprinkler and alarm systems.

Keep fire drill records. HHSC may request the last 12 months with an evacuation waiver (§553.259(e)(2)(C)(vii)). Drill frequency should be confirmed from Subchapter D and the unread parts of §553.275.
Emergency and evacuation procedures are a required topic in the 4-hr orientation for all staff (§553.253(d)(1)(F)).

Staff must be sufficient to ensure safe evacuation (§553.253(c)(3)(F)). A Fire Marshal notification (Form 1127) and Fire Suppression notification (Form 1129) are required if a resident's evacuation capability changes.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Maintain a written infection prevention and control policy (§553.261(f)(1)). Comply with the special waste rules at 25 TAC Chapter 1, Subchapter K.
Immediately report any resident with a reportable disease (25 TAC Chapter 97, Subchapter A) to the local health authority and follow its direction.

Written procedures must cover: monitoring key infectious agents and multidrug-resistant organisms; PPE and hand hygiene; cleaning and disinfecting surfaces such as door knobs, handrails and light switches; universal precautions; and daily removal of soiled items (§553.261(f)(5)).
Keep a written policy and procedures for a rapid influenza diagnostic test for residents with flu-like symptoms (§553.261(f)(6)).
Handle, store, process and transport linens to prevent spread of infection. Use universal precautions for all residents.

Exclude employees with a communicable disease transmissible through food handling or direct care for the period of communicability. A food service employee with a communicable disease or infected wound may not work in food service (§553.261(e)(12),(f)(4)(A)).

policies.title: Smoking, Visitors and Pets
state_specifics: Residents may have unrestricted communication and personal visitation with any person of their choice at any reasonable hour, including family and representatives of advocacy groups (§553.267(a)(3)(J)). Residents have a private place for receiving visitors (§553.267(a)(3)(R)).
HHSC and local authority employees must be admitted as needed to serve a resident (§553.267(c)). Ombudsmen follow RR-03.

Tobacco products may not be used in food preparation and service areas (§553.261(e)(14)). Smoking elsewhere follows NFPA 101 and Subchapter D; state the facility's smoking areas in the admission agreement.
Providers may maintain an environment free of weapons and drugs (§553.267(b)(2)(I)).
Pets and service animals that live in the facility must be covered in the evacuation plan (§553.275(i)(2)(B)).

policies.title: Food Service and Therapeutic Diets
state_specifics: Designate a person responsible for the total food service (§553.261(e)(1)).
At least 3 meals or equivalent daily, at regular times, with no more than 16 hours between a substantial evening meal and breakfast. Exceptions must be approved by HHSC.
Plan menus one week ahead and follow them. Document variations. Menus must be balanced and nutritious. Keep menus as served for 30 days.
Physician-ordered therapeutic diets are provided per the service plan. Diets that a layperson cannot customarily prepare must be calculated by a qualified dietitian.
Keep at least a 4-day supply of staple foods and a 1-day supply of perishable foods on the premises.
Staffing must be sufficient to prepare and serve meals that meet each resident's nutritional and special dietary needs (§553.253(c)(3)(C)).

policies.title: Food Safety and Sanitation
state_specifics: Potentially hazardous foods are held at 45°F or below. Hot food is held at 140°F or above. Reheated food reaches 165°F. Refrigerators are 41°F or below, freezers 0°F or below, with thermometers in the warmest area (§553.261(e)(8)–(9)).
Food comes from sources compliant with food laws. Food removed from its original container is sealed, labeled and dated if perishable.
Use effective hair restraints, handwashing after using the lavatory, sanitary dishwashing, and cleaned, rinsed and sanitized surfaces. No tobacco in food areas.
Facilities that house 17 or more residents must comply with 25 TAC Chapter 228 (Retail Food) and local health ordinances (§553.261(e)(18)).

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
state_specifics: Provide an activity or social program at least weekly (§553.261(d)).
Residents may take part in social, religious or community groups and practice their chosen religion (§553.267(a)(3)(B),(C)).
The comprehensive assessment records involvement patterns and preferred activities (§553.259(b)(1)(H)).
STAR+PLUS members: offer at least 4 social activities a week (Handbook §§7250–7252).

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance
state_specifics: Staff must be sufficient to maintain order, safety and cleanliness and to assist with laundry (§553.253(c)(3)(A),(D)).
Clean and disinfect environmental surfaces. Remove soiled items from the environment at least daily. Handle linens to prevent infection (§553.261(f)(5),(7)).
Residents have a safe and decent living environment (§553.267(a)(3)(F)).
Maintain the building and fire protection systems to Subchapter D standards.

policies.title: Transportation (Non-Emergency and Evacuation)
state_specifics: Chapter 553 as retrieved has no stand-alone non-emergency transportation rule. Facility-provided transportation is a charge disclosed in the admission agreement (§553.259(a)(2)).

Evacuation transportation is one of the 8 core functions of the emergency plan. The plan includes the procedure for safely transporting residents and notifying drivers, and the employer of any non-facility driver, of the evacuation (§553.275(a)(5)(B), (c)(1), (g)(5)(G)).
Sufficient trained staff must accompany evacuating residents and remain with them (§553.275(i)(2)(D)(ii)).
Residents may leave the facility temporarily or permanently, subject to contractual or financial obligations (§553.267(a)(3)(Z)).

policies.title: Staffing Levels and Supervision
state_specifics: Chapter 553 sets no numeric ratio. Staffing ratios must be based on residents' needs as identified in their service plans (§553.253(c)(1)).
An attendant must be in the facility at all times when residents are in the facility. Attendants may also perform other functions the facility requires (§553.253(b)).
Night shift: small Type A, staff immediately available; large Type A, immediately available and awake; Type B (any size), immediately available and awake.
Disclose the normal 24-hr staffing pattern to prospective residents and families before admission, and post it monthly (§§553.253(c)(2), 553.271(8)).
Staff must be sufficient to maintain order, safety and cleanliness, assist with medications, prepare meals, assist with laundry, supervise residents and ensure safe evacuation.
Full-time attendants must be at least 18 or a high school graduate.

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: Comply with HSC Chapter 250. Before hire, search the Employee Misconduct Registry (EMR) and HHSC Nurse Aide Registry (NAR). Do not hire or retain anyone listed as unemployable or convicted of an offense that bars employment under HSC §250.006 (§553.257(b)).
Repeat EMR and NAR searches at least every 12 months. Keep the results in the personnel file.
If the applicant lived in another state in the past 5 years, run a name-based criminal history check in each state. The person may be hired pending results but may not have direct resident contact.
Give the employee EMR notification per 26 TAC §561.3.
Obtain a signed disclosure statement on §250.006 convictions and residence in another state (§553.257(a)(7)).
Suspend, and do not reinstate during appeals, an employee HHSC finds engaged in reportable conduct (§553.257(b)(8)).

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
state_specifics: Document that staff are competent to provide personal care before assuming responsibilities (§553.253(d)).

4-hr orientation before any job responsibilities: reporting abuse and neglect; confidentiality; universal precautions; conditions to notify the manager about; resident rights; emergency and evacuation procedures.

Attendants: 16 hrs of on-the-job supervision and training within the first 16 hrs of employment after orientation. Topics: ADL assistance, health conditions, accident prevention, emergency first aid (Heimlich, falls, lacerations, sudden changes), disruptive behavior, behavior management, fall prevention.
Direct care staff: 6 documented hrs/yr by hire date, including 1 hr fall prevention and 1 hr behavior management, competency-based.
Nurses, CNAs and medication aides: annual geriatric in-service from the §553.253(d)(4) topic list.
Alzheimer's/dementia training per §553.254. Medication aide permit renewal yearly with 7 hrs CE after the first renewal.

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: Screen all employees for TB within 2 weeks of employment and annually per CDC guidelines. Outside-resource contractors must provide evidence on request (§553.261(f)(4)(C)).
Maintain written communicable disease policies for employees and residents covering TB screening (§553.261(f)(4)).
Exclude employees with a communicable disease transmissible through food handling or direct care for the period of communicability.
Keep evidence of compliance with local and state health codes on employee and resident health status.
Keep initial TB screening documentation in the personnel file (§553.257(a)(4)).

policies.title: Employee and Contractor Vaccination Policy
state_specifics: Maintain a written policy to protect residents from vaccine-preventable diseases under HSC Chapter 224 (§553.261(f)(9)).

The policy must: require employees and direct-care contractors to receive the vaccines the facility specifies based on their risk; specify the vaccines; include verification procedures; include procedures to exempt for CDC-identified medical contraindications or precautions; state protective measures for exempt employees; prohibit retaliation against medically exempt employees; require a written or electronic record of compliance or exemption; and state disciplinary actions for non-compliance.
The policy may also allow exemption for reasons of conscience, including religious beliefs, and may bar exempt staff from resident contact during a public health disaster.
Keep each employee's compliance or exemption in the personnel file (§553.257(a)(5)).

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Keep current, complete personnel records available for HHSC review (§553.257(a)). Contents: criminal history documentation; annual EMR and NAR results; TB screening; vaccine compliance or exemption; the signed statement on criminal liability for failure to report; the signed disclosure statement.

Also keep documentation of orientation, 16-hr on-the-job training, annual education hours and competency (§553.253(d)); the manager's 24-hr course evidence with content, hours, dates and provider (§553.253(a)(2)(A)(iii)); Alzheimer's training certificates (§553.254(e)); and the medication aide permit and any RN delegation records.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Staff may not abuse, neglect or exploit residents. Financial exploitation of $25 or more is reportable conduct (§553.257(b)(9)(C)).
Staff may not retaliate against any person who files a complaint or provides information (§553.273(e)).
Staff acknowledge their duty to report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation and their potential criminal liability (§553.273(f)).
Residents may refuse to perform services for the facility except as contracted (§553.267(a)(3)(V)). Respect privacy, dignity and personal property.
Training topics include promoting dignity, independence and choice, resident rights, and conflict resolution (§553.253(d)(3)).

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
state_specifics: Resident records contain: the standard admission form, assessments, the service plan, physician orders, advance directives, the physician exam within 30 days before or 14 days after admission (unless exempt, including Christian Scientists), health professionals' service documentation, and guardianship papers (§553.265(a)(2)).
Records are confidential, safeguarded, and available to residents, their legal representatives and HHSC.

Request the guardianship court order and letters at admission, upon learning of a guardian, and at each annual assessment. Make at least one follow-up request within 30 days. Keep the results and copies.
Keep a simple financial record of charges and of any personal funds held. Issue receipts on request.
Keep menus as served for 30 days, medication profile and missed-dose records, monthly self-administration counseling records, AEM forms in the clinical record, and incident reports.
The retrieved §553.265 sets no fixed retention period for resident records. Set the period in facility policy with counsel (the HIPAA documentation period is 6 years).

policies.title: Required Reports and Notifications to HHSC and Others
state_specifics: Abuse, neglect, exploitation: oral report immediately to HHSC (1-800-458-9858) and law enforcement. Written investigation report to the HHSC state office no later than the 5th calendar day (§553.273).
Notify HHSC before immediate termination of a resident who is a serious threat (§553.267(b)(2)(C)).
Placement forms (1124, 1125, 1126) or evacuation waiver packet to the HHSC regional office within 10 working days (§553.259(e)).
Notify the HHSC regional office and EMC immediately after deciding to shelter in place or evacuate (§553.275(h)(2),(i)(2)(D)).
Report resident reportable diseases immediately to the local health authority (§553.261(f)(3)).
License renewal at least 45 days before expiration, and approval before adding beds (§§553.33, 553.39, 553.47).
STAR+PLUS: report significant changes to the MCO by the next business day.
Report incidents through TULIP or the 800-458-9858 intake line.
